Rawi · first run

From download to your first dictation in seven steps

Every screenshot on this page is the real setup window, rendered from the current build of Rawi, in each state it can be in. The rail on the left of the window ticks steps off by itself: permissions are granted in System Settings, so Rawi keeps looking rather than waiting for you to come back and say so.

Step by step

First launch

1

Welcome

Intro

What it asks

Nothing yet. One sentence on what Rawi does, and that your voice never leaves the Mac.

What Rawi checks

Nothing. The rail on the left starts checking everything the moment the window opens, every 1.5 seconds.

Done when

You press Get started.

2

Microphone

Required

What it asks

Allow shows the macOS microphone prompt, with the reason already on screen: Rawi listens only while you hold your key, and deletes the recording once it is transcribed.

What Rawi checks

Whether macOS reports the microphone as authorised.

If…

  • You clicked Don’t Allow before

    macOS never shows its prompt twice. The button becomes Open Settings and the line says to turn Rawi on there; the tick appears as soon as you do.

Done when

The microphone is authorised. Required: dictation cannot work without it.

Accessibility not granted

3

Typing for you

Recommended

What it asks

Open Settings shows the macOS Accessibility prompt, opens Privacy & Security at the Accessibility list, and reveals Rawi.app in Finder so it can be dragged in.

What Rawi checks

Whether Rawi is trusted for Accessibility.

If…

  • You skip it

    Rawi still works: it copies what you said and the pill shows “Copied · ⌘V to paste”. You also lose learning spellings from your corrections and field-level destinations.

Done when

Accessibility is on. Recommended, not required.

4

Speech model

Required

What it asks

Three things, checked separately: whisper.cpp, the transcription model (Large v3 Turbo, 547 MB) and the language detector (141 MB) that lets one key serve English and Arabic.

What Rawi checks

whisper.cpp on the PATH or in Homebrew; each model file in Application Support/Rawi/models.

If…

  • whisper.cpp is missing

    Rawi cannot install it for you. The row shows brew install whisper-cpp with a Copy command button; the tick appears once Homebrew finishes.

  • Models are missing

    Download fetches whatever is missing, one after the other, with a progress bar per model. An interrupted download never leaves a half file that looks installed.

  • A download fails

    The reason appears under the rows in red and Download comes back.

Done when

whisper.cpp and both models are present. Required.

5

Polish

Optional

What it asks

Whether to use the local model that removes filler, applies spoken corrections and writes run-ons as sentences. It runs on Ollama.

What Rawi checks

Whether Ollama answers on this Mac, and which of the models the config names it already has.

If…

  • Ollama is not installed

    Get Ollama opens ollama.com. Use polish turns it on; Skip turns it off and moves on, and Rawi types exactly what it heard.

  • Ollama is running

    Each model is listed with what it is for: English polish, Arabic and mixed speech, transforms. Download models pulls the missing ones with progress.

  • Everything is present

    The step ticks itself.

Done when

Polish is ready, or you chose to skip it. Optional.

⌥ chosen, Input Monitoring just granted

6

Your key

Required

What it asks

Click the field and press the key you want: a combination such as ⌃⌥Space, or a single ⌥, ⌘, ⌃ or fn. Hold to speak, double-tap for hands-free.

What Rawi checks

Whether Input Monitoring is granted, which a single key needs.

If…

  • A single key without Input Monitoring

    Refused, with the reason under the field in red. Combinations work without the permission.

  • Input Monitoring granted during setup

    The key listener only learns about it on launch, so Restart Rawi appears.

Done when

You press Continue. There is always a key.

Your first dictation

7

Try it

Required

What it asks

Click in the box, hold your key, say something, let go. Your words appear in the box, through the same path they will take in every other app.

What Rawi checks

Whether anything has been typed in the box, and whether dictation can work at all.

If…

  • The microphone or speech model is not ready

    A red line says to finish those steps first.

Done when

Text appears. Finish saves that setup is complete and closes the window.

Rendered from Rawi’s own SwiftUI setup view at build 2026-09-15, in dark appearance. The walkthrough shows the states the view is built to handle; the permission prompts themselves are macOS’s and are not pictured.
